observations: Photos show a removed vehicle drivetrain/gearbox assembly on a workshop floor, with many attached hoses/wiring and a large transmission case.
No clear readable brand/model markings are visible on the gearbox/transmission casing in the provided photos.
The assembly appears used and dusty/dirty; some components look disconnected/loose (typical for removed units), but condition details (leaks, cracks) are not confirmable from these angles.
Seller text claims it is an American drive gearbox for Ford Econoline E150/E250/E350 V8, but this is not verifiable from the photos shown.

claims.claim: American drive Gearbox for Ford Econoline E150 E250 E350 V8
claims.evidence: Photos do not show a readable Ford/Econoline application tag, transmission code, or model number that ties it to E150/E250/E350 V8.
No test/inspection sheet, video of operation, or readable transmission code/condition indicators are shown.

risks.risk: Wrong transmission type/spec (pin count, 2WD vs 4WD, automatic vs manual, gear ratios) leading to non-fit or non-function.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear close-up photo of the transmission identification tag/label and/or stamped transmission code on the case (and the connector/pin count area).
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst-case: not guaranteed to match your vehicle spec (treated like a generic used gearbox with unknown compatibility).

risks.risk: Not working / internal failure (slipping, no engagement, torque converter issues) even if it looks intact.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video of the gearbox being tested (engaging gears and reverse) or a mechanic’s test report with results.

risks.risk: Missing parts or incomplete kit (sensors, harness connectors, cooler lines, mounting brackets, bolts).
risks.proof: Ask for a photo inventory laid out on the floor showing all included parts (sensors, harness plugs, dipstick/lines if applicable, mounting hardware).
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst-case: may be missing small parts (assume buyer must source extras).

risks.risk: Damage during removal/shipping (cracked case, bent shafts, broken mounts) not obvious from these angles.
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of the bellhousing/adapter area, mounting points, and any visible cracks/impact points.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst-case: possible damage not confirmed.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the transmission ID tag/stamped code on the gearbox case (the exact code that determines compatibility).
Photo showing connector(s) and the pin count (or a close-up of the harness plug area).
Video of the gearbox test (engagement of gears/reverse) or a written mechanic test result.
Inventory photos of all included components (sensors, harness, cooler lines, mounts, bolts/hardware).
response.reason: The photos show a used gearbox assembly, but there is no readable identification (transmission code/application) and no proof of testing. Without that, the correct match and working status—which drive the price—cannot be determined reliably.
